LigaDesign system v0.1

Liga design system

Everything the Liga app is built from: tokens, components and patterns. Dark first, light as a full second theme. Built on the Office 8-Ball system, standardised and made sport neutral, with feedback components taken from the Simon's Dashboard DS.

Logging takes five secondsOpponent, winner, done. Everything else is optional and comes after.
Black and white firstColour is earned. It means something: win, live, crown, brand. Never decoration.
Big where it mattersRatings, names on the live screen and celebration moments go large. Everyday UI stays calm and dense.
Sport neutralNo balls, nets or tables in the core UI. The sport shows up as an icon and a word.
One system, two themesComponents only read semantic tokens. A theme swaps the tokens, never the components.

Foundations

Colour

Three layers. Primitives are raw values, semantic tokens say what a value is for and swap with the theme, components only read semantic tokens. Neutrals carry almost every screen, one violet accent marks the brand, and meaning colours stay rare so a win or a live match pops. Every colour is used solid, never tinted or transparent.

The app icon, the league mark, the unread dot, your own row marker, one hero action per screen, and brand moments like onboarding and the paywall.

As text on dark (3.0:1 is too low), tinted, faded, or as a win or live signal.

Primary actions

Stay white on dark and black on light. Violet is the accent, not the button colour. Text on violet is always white.

Typography

Two families. Sora 800 for display, always uppercase with tight tracking. Inter for everything else. Numbers are always tabular. No italics, no text shadows, and no small uppercase labels with wide letter spacing.

Don't

Put a small label above a title, space out uppercase letters, or use italics for emphasis.

Spacing and radius

4 px base. Dense, like a feed: cards use 16 px padding, sheets 20 px, the screen gutter is 16 px. Corners get rounder as the surface gets bigger.

Surfaces and depth

Depth comes from stepping up the surface, not from shadows. Only floating things (tab bar, menus, the log button) cast a shadow. No borders on cards.

Icons

Lucide line icons at stroke 2.25, so they hold their weight next to Sora and bold Inter. Four sizes, one rule: an icon supports a label, it never replaces one the user has to understand. Emoji only for badges, reactions and fun awards.

Motion

One curve, five durations. Everything eases in and out on cubic-bezier(.65, 0, .35, 1), never overshoots and never bounces. Everyday UI stays under 400 ms, celebrations may take a full scene of 1.2 s, and every animation has a calm reduced motion version.

Every demo replays with its button. Tap Replay all to run the whole system at once.

Your device asks for reduced motion, so these demos finish instantly.

Do
  • Use the token durations and var(--ease) for every transition.
  • Animate transform and opacity of neutral surfaces, keep it at 60 fps.
  • Let one thing lead. The rest follows with a short stagger.
Don't
  • Use springs, overshoot or bounce, even in celebrations.
  • Fade a brand or meaning colour to make it lighter.
  • Make the user wait on a scene to keep going.

Do
  • Keep a pill to one or two words and one meaning colour.
  • Show at most two pills per row, the most important first.
  • Make active chips a solid primary fill with a cross to remove.
Don't
  • Make a pill tappable. If it does something, it is a chip or a button.
  • Use a pale tint with a coloured border for any state.
  • Use meaning colours for decoration, green always means a win.

Segmented control and tabs

A segmented control switches a view in place, 2 to 4 options of equal width with centred labels. Tabs split a screen into sections, like a profile, and may scroll. Both move one solid indicator, 280 ms ease in out.

      PatternUse whenAvoid whenTiming
      SkeletonFirst load of a screen or card whose shape you knowData is already cached, show it insteadOnly after 300 ms, then crossfade 280 ms

      How rating works

      Everyone starts at 1 000. Beat someone rated higher and you gain more; lose to someone lower and you drop more.

      You 1 237 beat Mira 1 302+21
      1 of 3
      Popover, a tip pointing at its source
      Bottom sheet

      Log a match, send a challenge, filter a list. Swipe down, tap the scrim or close to dismiss.

      • Radius24 top
      • HeightFits content, max 88%
      • ActionsOne primary at the bottom
      Dialog

      Only for steps that cannot be undone. The safe choice is always one tap away.

      • Width360 max
      • ActionsTwo, stacked
      • Scrim tapCancels
      Action menu

      Secondary actions for one item. Destructive goes last, after a divider, in red.

      • Rows44 tall, up to 6
      • Radius16, items 8
      • ScrimNone, tap outside
      Popover

      A short tip that points at what it explains. Never holds a form or a choice that matters.

      • Width280 max
      • TextTwo lines, one action
      • DismissTap anywhere
      Do
      • Keep the screen behind visible, so people know where they are
      • Put the main action at the bottom, in thumb reach
      • Say exactly what will happen: "Delete match", not "OK"
      Don't
      • Stack a sheet on a sheet, or open a dialog from a menu just to confirm sharing
      • Use a dialog for a form or a choice of more than two
      • Hide the only way to close behind a swipe
      LayerSurfaceEnterExitFocus
      Bottom sheet--overlay, scrimSlide up 280 ms, ease in outSlide down 180 msMoves to the title, returns to the trigger
      Dialog--overlay, scrimFade and scale from 97%, 280 msFade 180 msLands on the safe button
      Action menu--overlay, float shadowFade and grow from the anchor, 180 msFade 120 msFirst item, arrow keys move
      Popover--overlay, float shadowFade 180 msFade 120 msRead by screen readers as a note

      Do
      • Show every round at once on tablet and desktop, scroll one round per swipe on phones.
      • Name the match an empty seat waits for, like Winner semi 2.

        Do

        Swipe, refresh, load more

        Rows in your own match history swipe left to reveal two quick actions. Every action also lives in the long press menu, so swiping is never the only way. Feeds refresh with a pull from the top and load older items with a row at the bottom.

        Swipe action row

        • D7 DaveLost 6 to 10, 2 h ago −12
        • M5 MiraWon 10 to 8, yesterday +16
        • SK Sam and Kim2v2 with Ann, 3 days ago +9
        • J3 JoeWon 10 to 2, 5 h ago +7
        Long press for every actionHold a row for half a second, right click it, or focus it and press Enter. The menu opens next to the row.

        Swipe left or press the left arrow to reveal Rematch and Delete. Right arrow or Escape closes.

        Matches older than 24 h cannot be deleted, so the 2v2 row only shows Rematch. Delete always offers Undo for 6 s.

          Motion tokens

          Five durations and one curve cover everything. Pick the shortest one that still reads. Scenes are the only place that may run longer than 400 ms.

          One curve, ease in out. --ease: cubic-bezier(.65, 0, .35, 1). Slow start, fast middle, slow end. It never goes past 1, so nothing overshoots or settles back. No spring and no bounce curves anywhere, also not in Expo (use Easing.bezier(.65, 0, .35, 1)).

          TokenValueUsed for
          --d-press120 msButton and row press, scale to .97 and back
          --d-fast180 msHover, colour change, toast in and out, unread dot, reduced motion fades
          --d-base280 msToggle, segmented indicator, tab bar slide, sheet up, list rows, skeleton crossfade, reaction pop
          --d-slow400 msRank swap, progress fill, crown drop, anything that travels far
          --d-scene1200 msCelebration scenes, the longest step, the whole scene ends by 1.4 s
          --mo-count800 msNumber count up for rating, coins and bounty
          --mo-stagger40 msDelay between rows or tiles appearing
          --mo-rise8 pxHow far things rise when they appear
          --ease.65, 0, .35, 1Every animation, no exceptions

          Reduced motion

          When the phone asks for reduced motion, nothing moves, scales or turns. The final state appears with one fade on --d-base. Numbers show their final value, confetti and flashes are skipped. Use the preview switch at the top of this group to see it.

          Micro interactionsInstantToggle, segment and tab change state at once, the stage fades in 280 ms
          Toast, Elo deltaFade onlySame timing, no rise
          Rank swapFadeRows swap places in one frame, the list fades in
          Match savedCrossfadeFinal screen with +14, +20 and the new rank fades in
          Crown takenCrossfadeGold card, crown and bounty already in place
          Challenge sentCrossfadeCard already landed, all stakes visible
          Badge unlockedCrossfadeFull ring, no turn, no confetti
          Cup championCrossfadeTrophy, rays and name in place, no confetti

          Gamification

          Level and streak

          Every match, quest and reaction earns XP. Levels are hexagons in solid brand, milestones every ten levels turn gold. The bar fills with a green gain chunk first, then the brand fill catches up; crossing the top flashes the whole card brand for one beat, never a bounce.

          Badges and achievements

          Season emblems

          Every finished season leaves one faceted crest on your profile. The metal is the placement, the big number is the season, the medallion on the tip repeats the place in words. One SVG symbol, three variables per finish, solid metal with neutral light and shade facets.

          Finishes

          GoldFinished #1
          SilverFinished #2
          BronzeFinished #3
          Participant#4 and below
          Live seasonNow #3, 20% done
          LockedStarts Jan 5

          Gold and silver carry black numbers, bronze, participant and live carry white. The live crest draws season progress along its rim in solid white.

          Sizes

          XL 160 pxReward, season recap
          L 96 pxTrophy case
          M 56 pxLists, profile
          S 28 pxInline
          How it degradesXL and L show everything: rim bevels, face facets, the S prefix and the place medallion.M drops the medallion and centres the number, the place moves to the text next to it.S keeps only the crest and the season digit, 22 to 32 px, always next to a name.

          Achievement collection

          The full set in one grid: earned medals in full colour, goals in progress inside a ring, locked ones with a hint so people know what to chase, and secrets that stay hidden until they happen. When one unlocks, the moment gets a short celebration.

            Rules

            Do
            • Use only semantic tokens in components
            • Use colour solid, with its fixed text partner
            • Keep one primary button per screen
            • Keep touch targets at least 44 px
            • Give every icon button an accessible name
            • Use ease in out, no overshoot
            • Show the stakes before a match is played
            Don't
            • Tint or fade the brand or meaning colours
            • Use red for a loss
            • Use pale pills with a coloured border
            • Use italics or text shadows
            • Put a small label above a title
            • Space out uppercase letters
            • Use dashes, dots or slashes to separate text, use gap or a line break
            • Draw sport objects in the core UI

            Tokens for the app

            The Expo app reads the same values from tokens.json, generated from tokens.css. Names match one to one: --surface-2 becomes color.surface2.
